samples.summary: Phase 25's design doc still documents the old `spec-to-pr.mjs review` contract (token-required, warn-and-skip, "a convenience, not authority") that this change deletes
samples.evidence: harness-engineering.md:2403-2406 reads: "**Local review is a convenience, not authority:** `spec-to-pr.mjs review` runs the same lenses over the working diff, but needs `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and degrades to a warn-and-skip when it is absent. The authoritative panel is still the cloud one". This change removes the skip entirely (`ambientAuthNotice` + `cmdReview` now proceed on the logged-in session), and both the new `.claude/commands/self-review.md` and `docs/design/agentic-dev-loop.md` §1.1 argue the opposite position — for an ordinary branch the local run is the *only* machine review. CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, `.claude/commands/spec-to-pr.md` and agentic-dev-loop.md were all updated; the Phase 25 doc that is the cited authority for this exact subcommand was not, so the repo now states both contracts. Per CONTRIBUTING's design-doc discipline the canonical subsystem doc should be folded, not left contradicting.

samples.summary: `normalizeRebuttals` re-implements the `agent-review-` lens-prefix strip that `rebuttal.mjs` already owns, and the local path skips the rest of that module's record normalization
samples.evidence: `rebuttal.mjs:203` already does `str(d.lens).trim().replace(/^agent-review-/, "")` inside `parseRebuttalComment`, and `sanitizeRebuttal` (rebuttal.mjs:99-107) additionally trims and `neutral()`s `summary`/`claim`/`evidence` before a record reaches the panel. The new `normalizeRebuttals` in spec-to-pr.mjs copies only the prefix rule and writes the record straight to `rebuttals.json` for the panel. Two independent definitions of "what a lens id is" can diverge (the cloud's is the one the panel partitions on), and the local record bypasses the normalization every cloud record gets. Exporting/reusing the existing helper from rebuttal.mjs would state it once.

samples.summary: ~600 lines of self-review round-store, temp-directory hardening and terminal rendering land in `spec-to-pr.mjs`, whose own new header argues the `review` subcommand does not belong to that file's concern
samples.evidence: The new header block (spec-to-pr.mjs:20-26) states "THE `review` SUBCOMMAND IS NOT AGENT-TRACK-ONLY, despite this file's name", and the task record (docs/tasks/active/20260917-self-review-loop-todo.md:67) names the same mismatch as "the whole reason the capability reads as unavailable to hand-driven work" — then resolves it with a slash command rather than a module. The result is that a file about spec→handoff now carries the round store (`roundsIn`/`nextRound`/`pickLatestVerdicts`/`roundsOnDisk`), a filesystem-safety policy (`unsafeBaseReason`/`ownedPathChain`), rebuttal normalization and a terminal renderer, none of which `handoff` touches. A sibling `scripts/agent/self-review.mjs` that `spec-to-pr.mjs review` delegates to would put the loop at the layer its own docs place it. Behaviour is unaffected, so the cost is cohesion only.

samples.summary: The task record's Verification and Known-limitations sections describe behaviour this same branch no longer has (`--round 4` "still runs"; detached HEAD shares one round directory)
samples.evidence: Line 85 records "`--round 4` prints the bound advisory and still runs", but `roundBoundNotice` + `cmdReview` now REFUSE past `MAX_SELF_REVIEW_ROUNDS` unless `--force` (spec-to-pr.mjs, `if (notice && !args.force) return fail(...)`), and the branch's own test asserts the refusal. Line 186 lists "A detached HEAD shares one round directory (the branch name is `HEAD`)" as a known limitation, but `branchKey` in this diff fixes exactly that and is tested ("branchKey: a detached HEAD never keys the round store as `HEAD`"). The task record is the spec this change is judged against and CLAUDE.md step 6 expects it to be the record of what shipped; leaving two stale claims in it makes the record disagree with the code it documents.

samples.summary: §1.1 describes `carryForwardFindings` as "shared with the cloud's projection" and the loop as flatly "bounded at three rounds", omitting the mirrored-copy reality and the `--force` override
samples.evidence: The new §1.1 text says the loop "carries each round's still-gating findings into the next (`carryForwardFindings`, shared with the cloud's projection)". It is not shared: `agent-review-panel.yml` carries an inline `github-script` copy that cannot import the module (the diff's own drift-guard test in prior-findings.test.mjs exists precisely because "the two must agree by inspection"). §1.1 also states the bound without naming `--force`, which `.claude/commands/self-review.md` documents as the sanctioned way past it — so the canonical design doc understates the mechanism it describes. Four places now restate the loop rules (CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, self-review.md, this §), which is where that drift comes from.
